opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexandra Johnson (employee ID E003) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E003.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. As full-time staff, max is write unless role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, so admin is not permitted. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E003 (Alexandra Johnson) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: E003 (Alexandra Johnson) requested admin to Source Code. There is conflicting employment info: one note says full-time Analyst (max write; admin not allowed since Source Code is owned by Engineer), while the security note says E003 is a contractor with basic security training (max read; never admin). Given the security record (looked up in its database) shows contractor with basic training, the maximum permitted level is read. Requested admin exceeds read, so grant read.
